title: Axor Lab Artifact
description:
The portable, reproducible output of a Run (Suite Platform RFC §14) and the platform's user-facing noun — the UI says Artifact, never 'bundle'. It carries the suite, configuration, environment, agent identity, observations, traces, metrics, EvidenceCases, regressions, reproduce instructions, signatures and hashes.

DELIBERATELY A WRAPPER, not a superset: an artifact EMBEDS a bundle/v1 body verbatim rather than restating its fields. bundle/v1 is content-addressed and its hashes are already published, so restating its fields in a new shape would invalidate every existing hash; nesting it keeps `content_hash(artifact.bundle)` equal to the hash the bundle always had. A pre-Suite-Platform bundle therefore upgrades losslessly: wrap it, leave suite/evidence_cases/regressions empty, and every prior hash still verifies.

bundle.description: the reproducible core, embedded byte-for-byte: scenarios, conditions, tool manifests, environment, trials (with their metrics), aggregates, content hashes

suite.description: the RESOLVED suite manifest that produced this run — scenario_refs already resolved to bodies, so a later registry change cannot retroactively alter what this artifact says was run. Absent for an artifact produced from a hand-authored experiment with no suite.

agent_identity.description: the fingerprint of what actually ran. bundle.environment records the execution environment; this records the AGENT, which the RFC names as its own artifact component.

fingerprint.description: content hash over the agent's identity-bearing configuration

params_hash.description: hash of the inference params; a temperature change is an identity change

determinism.description: whether the agent's behaviour is fixed by (scenario, seed). A matched-pairs design requires 'deterministic'; a stochastic agent's arms are independent samples.

evidence_cases.description: investigations curated from this run's trials, travelling WITH the artifact so a reader gets the findings, not just the data

regressions.description: invariants pinned from this run, each carrying its own outcome history

reproduce.description: how to re-run this. The RFC lists reproduce instructions as a first-class artifact component precisely so reproduction is not folklore.

command.description: the exact CLI invocation, e.g. 'axor-lab run suite.axl --out ./bundle'

requires.description: what a reproducer must supply that the artifact cannot contain — model API credentials, a specific kernel build, a private dataset. An empty list is a CLAIM that the artifact is self-contained.

reproducibility.description: the honest ceiling. exact_replay = frozen traces recompute bit-identically; statistically_reproducible = a fresh live run should agree within CI; not_reproducible = traces were excluded (artifact.include_traces=false) or the environment cannot be recreated. A behavioural delta can never claim exact_replay (claims.md).

content_hashes.description: hashes over the artifact's own parts, including `bundle` as a whole. The embedded bundle keeps its own internal content_hashes untouched.

signature.description: optional author signature over the canonical artifact body

signed_ref.description: the content hash actually signed — a signature that does not name what it covers proves nothing
